expectations.text: Presents the incentive ranking with efficiency, effort, value and compliance-cost axes stated out loud, and names 'none, with results shared first with respondents' as the default.
expectations.evidence: No efficiency/effort/value/compliance axes are laid out and 'none, with results shared first' is never named as the default; it only ranks donation above raffle.

expectations.text: Ranks the prize draw low on compliance cost, naming contact data, a separate store and sweepstakes rules per jurisdiction.
expectations.evidence: 'contact data, a separate store and per-jurisdiction rules apply.'

expectations.text: States that prize-draw effects on completes are small and inconsistent.
expectations.evidence: 'The skill finds draw effects "small and inconsistent"'.

expectations.text: Refuses adding an email field to the survey response table and requires any contact collection in a separate form under its own consent.
expectations.evidence: 'Do not add an email field to the survey... separate form with no join key'.

expectations.text: Recommends a fixed donation per complete as the next rung before paid responses, given the near date and the shortfall.
expectations.evidence: 'A donation ranks above a raffle... The cheaper version (recommended)'.

expectations.text: Warns that any public incentive draws bots and machine-written answers and requires switching on fraud checks before announcing: an attention or consistency check, a trap option nobody can have used, and detection of templated open text.
expectations.evidence: Lists an attention check, a trap option and a salted IP hash, but does not mention templated open text detection.
